claim: KCBP (kinesin-like calmodulin-binding protein) occurs solely within the plant kingdom.
source: KCBP (kinesin-like calmodulin-binding protein) occurs solely within the plant kingdom, and uniquely in the kinesin superfamily.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript about the taxonomic distribution of KCBP.

claim: KCBP has a C-terminal motor head.
source: KCBP has a C-terminal motor head, beyond which locates a calmodulin-binding domain (CBD) at the extreme end of the C-terminus
evidence: This is a direct statement about the structural organization of KCBP.

claim: The calmodulin-binding domain (CBD) is only found in KCBP and the sea urchin kinesin KinC among kinesins.
source: beyond which locates a calmodulin-binding domain (CBD) at the extreme end of the C-terminus; besides KCBP, the CBD is only found in the sea urchin kinesin KinC.
evidence: This is a direct statement comparing KCBP to other kinesins regarding the CBD domain.

claim: KCBP contains a MyTH4-FERM tandem in its N-terminal tail region.
source: KCBP also contains a MyTH4-FERM tandem, which only occurs in several myosin families outside the plant kingdom, in its tail region at the N-terminus (NT)
evidence: This is a direct statement about the domain structure of KCBP.

claim: The MyTH4-FERM tandem only occurs in several myosin families outside the plant kingdom.
source: KCBP also contains a MyTH4-FERM tandem, which only occurs in several myosin families outside the plant kingdom, in its tail region at the N-terminus (NT)
evidence: This is a direct statement about the distribution of the MyTH4-FERM tandem in other proteins.

claim: KCBP has long been regarded as a chimera of kinesin with a myosin.
source: thus, KCBP has long been regarded as a chimera of kinesin with a myosin (Abdel-Ghany et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: KCBP was first isolated as a novel calmodulin-binding protein with a kinesin motor domain using biotinylated calmodulin as a probe.
source: Using biotinylated calmodulin as a probe, KCBP was firstly isolated as a novel calmodulin-binding protein with a kinesin motor domain (Reddy et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The CBD of KCBP binds calcium/calmodulin, which negatively regulates KCBP motor activity.
source: In vitro biochemical assays showed that the CBD of KCBP binds calcium/calmodulin, which negatively regulates KCBP motor activity, and that the N-terminal tail, including the MyTH4-FERM domain, could co-sediment with MTs (Narasimhulu and Reddy, 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous in vitro biochemical studies.

claim: The N-terminal tail of KCBP, including the MyTH4-FERM domain, could co-sediment with MTs.
source: In vitro biochemical assays showed that the CBD of KCBP binds calcium/calmodulin, which negatively regulates KCBP motor activity, and that the N-terminal tail, including the MyTH4-FERM domain, could co-sediment with MTs (Narasimhulu and Reddy, 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous in vitro biochemical studies.

claim: The ZWICHEL (ZWI) gene encodes the KCBP protein.
source: Interestingly, genetic analysis of the zwichel (zwi) mutants, which have a shortened stalk and only two branches, revealed that the ZWICHEL (ZWI) gene encodes the KCBP protein (Hülskamp et al., 1994; Oppenheimer et al., 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous genetic studies.

claim: Zwichel (zwi) mutants have a shortened stalk and only two branches.
source: Interestingly, genetic analysis of the zwichel (zwi) mutants, which have a shortened stalk and only two branches, revealed that the ZWICHEL (ZWI) gene encodes the KCBP protein (Hülskamp et al., 1994; Oppenheimer et al., 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous genetic studies.

claim: KCBP was detected in mitotic MT arrays such as the preprophase band, the spindle, and the phragmoplast in various plants.
source: KCBP was detected in mitotic MT arrays such as the preprophase band, the spindle, and the phragmoplast in various plants, indicating that it may play a role in cell division (Bowser and Reddy, 1997; Smirnova et al., 1998; Preuss et al., 2003; Buschmann et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of function in KCBP only produces a noticeable phenotype in trichomes.
source: Nevertheless, loss of function in KCBP only produces a noticeable phenotype in trichomes, which are less-branched and contain shortened stalks and swollen, stunted branches (Oppenheimer et al., 1997)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous genetic studies.

claim: Loss of function in KCBP results in trichomes that are less-branched and contain shortened stalks and swollen, stunted branches.
source: Nevertheless, loss of function in KCBP only produces a noticeable phenotype in trichomes, which are less-branched and contain shortened stalks and swollen, stunted branches (Oppenheimer et al., 1997)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous genetic studies.

claim: GFP-KCBP localizes to puncta along cortical MTs in both pavement cells and hypocotyl cells.
source: Notably, we found that GFP-KCBP localizes to puncta along cortical MTs in both pavement cells and hypocotyl cells (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, Video 1, Video 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: Most GFP-KCBP proteins dwell on or move along cortical MTs as discrete particles for a short time (15.9 s, n = 647).
source: Most GFP-KCBP proteins dwell on or move along cortical MTs as discrete particles for a short time (15.9 s, n = 647)
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative analysis of live-cell imaging data.

claim: Only a small portion of GFP-KCBP particles remain immobilized on MTs for longer times.
source: only a small portion of GFP-KCBP particles remain immobilized on MTs for longer times (Video 1, Video 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in videos.

claim: KCBP exhibits short-lived and poorly processive movement.
source: Kymograph analysis further confirmed the short-lived and poorly processive nature of KCBP movement (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: This statement is supported by kymograph analysis shown in figures.

claim: The short-lived and poorly processive nature of KCBP movement is characteristic of non-processive motors of the kinesin-14 subfamily.
source: Kymograph analysis further confirmed the short-lived and poorly processive nature of KCBP movement (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2C), which is the characteristic of non-processive motors of the kinesin-14 subfamily (Fink et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature on kinesin-14 motors.

claim: KCBP moves at an average velocity of 0.68 μm/min (n = 647).
source: The distributions indicated that, upon fitting to an exponential line, the motor moved at an average velocity of 0.68 μm/min (n = 647) (Figure 1C, Figure 1—source data 1)
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative analysis of live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: KCBP moves at an average run length of 0.18 μm (n = 647).
source: and at an average run length of 0.18 μm (n = 647) (Figure 1D, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative analysis of live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: KCBP likely acts as a non-processive motor to facilitate crosslinking or bundling during MT organization.
source: Taken together, these results indicated that KCBP likely acts as a non-processive motor to facilitate crosslinking or bundling during MT organization.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the motility data presented in the manuscript.

claim: KCBP largely colocalizes with cortical MTs in developing trichomes.
source: Indeed, we observed that KCBP largely colocalizes with cortical MTs in developing trichomes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: KCBP forms a gradient in the elongating trichome branch, with the highest density at the extreme apex.
source: Intriguingly, KCBP forms a gradient in the elongating trichome branch, with the highest density at the extreme apex, which is devoid of MTs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The extreme apex of the elongating trichome branch is devoid of MTs.
source: Intriguingly, KCBP forms a gradient in the elongating trichome branch, with the highest density at the extreme apex, which is devoid of MTs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: KCBP shows punctuate localization in a cortical gradient in developing trichomes, with the highest density at the extreme apex.
source: We observed punctuate KCBP localization in the cortical gradient in developing trichomes, with the highest density at the extreme apex (Figure 2A,D,G; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A; Video 3, Video 4).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: Transversely aligned MT arrays (transverse MT rings) form in a similar gradient with higher MT density towards the branch tip, but forming a MT-depleted zone at the extreme apex.
source: In GFP-TUB6-expressing trichomes at identical developmental stages, we observed transversely aligned MT arrays (transverse MT rings) in a similar gradient with higher MT density towards the branch tip, but forming a MT-depleted zone at the extreme apex (Figure 2B,E,H; Figure 2—figure supplement 2B; Video 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: KCBP largely colocalizes with cortical MTs along the trichome branch, but shows highest levels in the MT-depleted zone at the branch apex.
source: In consistent with the result from the double-labeling imaging (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), KCBP largely colocalizes with cortical MTs along the trichome branch, but shows highest levels in the MT-depleted zone at the branch apex (Figure 2A,B,G,H; Video 3, Video 4).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: KCBP accumulates at the branching site, which has a relatively sparse MT network.
source: We also found a similar distribution at the branching site where KCBP accumulates, but which has a relatively sparse MT network (Figure 2A,B,D,E; Video 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: GCP2 shows a tip-directed gradient, but with a GCP2-depleted zone at the extreme apexes of elongating branches.
source: Interestingly, we observed that, similar to MTs, GCP2 shows a tip-directed gradient, but with a GCP2-depleted zone at the extreme apexes of elongating branches (Figure 2—figure supplement 3; Video 5).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: F-actin forms thick bundles parallel to the long axis of elongating branches and extend from the stalk to the region near branch tips.
source: We observed that F-actin forms thick bundles parallel to the long axis of elongating branches and extend from the stalk to the region near branch tips, but also form a cap with fine, cortical F-actin mainly in a transverse pattern in the tip region (Figure 2C,F,I; Video 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: F-actin forms a cap with fine, cortical F-actin mainly in a transverse pattern in the tip region of elongating branches.
source: We observed that F-actin forms thick bundles parallel to the long axis of elongating branches and extend from the stalk to the region near branch tips, but also form a cap with fine, cortical F-actin mainly in a transverse pattern in the tip region (Figure 2C,F,I; Video 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: The transverse cortical F-actin cap occupies a larger area than the MT-depleted zone, but coincides with the area where KCBP accumulates.
source: Notably, the transverse cortical F-actin cap occupies a larger area than the MT-depleted zone, but coincides with the area where KCBP accumulates (Figure 2A–I).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The specific distribution of KCBP is tightly associated with the assembly of the required cytoskeletal organization for trichome branching and elongation.
source: Together, our observations suggest that the specific distribution of KCBP is tightly associated with the assembly of the required cytoskeletal organization for trichome branching and elongation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Wild-type Arabidopsis leaf trichome initiates from a bulging protodermal cell and then grows out into a cylindrical cell, which exhibits random organization of the MT array.
source: The wild-type Arabidopsis leaf trichome initiates from a bulging protodermal cell and then grows out into a cylindrical cell, which exhibits random organization of the MT array (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The random MT network shifts into a transverse MT array (rings) encircling the elongating cylindrical cell.
source: The random MT network shifts into a transverse MT array (rings) encircling the elongating cylindrical cell (Figure 3B).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: Most trichomes undergo two consecutive branching events to form the typical three-branch pattern.
source: Most trichomes undergo two consecutive branching events to form the typical three-branch pattern (Figure 3E,F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: During trichome branch elongation, cortical MTs shift to transverse rings with the typical tip-directed MT density gradient.
source: During trichome branch elongation, cortical MTs also shift to transverse rings with the typical tip-directed MT density gradient (Figure 3C–F).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: A MT-depleted zone occurs at the extreme apex of the elongating branch.
source: Intriguingly, a MT-depleted zone occurs at the extreme apex of the elongating branch (Figure 3D; Video 6).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: At the maturation stage, fully elongated trichome branches form a fine and pointed tip, and cortical MTs reorient to an oblique or longitudinal configuration.
source: At the maturation stage, fully elongated trichome branches form a fine and pointed tip, and cortical MTs reorient to an oblique or longitudinal configuration (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: In stage 2/3 kcbp-1 trichomes, formation of the transverse MT rings that encircle the incipient primary branch is impaired.
source: In stage 2/3 trichomes, formation of the transverse MT rings that encircle the incipient primary branch is impaired (H, I).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: In kcbp-1 trichomes, the MT-depleted zone is not well defined.
source: The 3-D reconstruction (the inset in I) of the incipient primary branch tip (outlined by the dotted box) shows that the MT-depleted zone is not well defined.
evidence: This statement is supported by 3D reconstruction imaging data shown in figures.

claim: In stage 3/4/5 kcbp-1 trichomes, transverse MT rings are present in a relatively loose distribution.
source: In stage 3/4/5 trichomes (J, K), transverse MT rings are present in a relatively loose distribution.
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The secondary branching does not occur in kcbp-1 trichomes, yielding a two-branch trichome.
source: Subsequently, the primary branching event takes place from the severely reduced stalk (Figure 3H,I), but the secondary branching does not occur, yielding a two-branch trichome (Figure 3J,K, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: In kcbp-1 trichomes, one branch elongates and forms a tip that is not as pointed as the wild type, whereas the growth of the other branch is impaired, producing a swollen and blunt tip.
source: Eventually, one branch elongates and forms a tip that is not as pointed as the wild type, whereas the growth of the other branch is impaired, producing a swollen and blunt tip (Figure 3K, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: KCBP is required to assemble the transverse MT rings encircling the elongating branch and formation of the MT-depleted zone.
source: Together, these observations indicated that KCBP is required to assemble the transverse MT rings encircling the elongating branch and formation of the MT-depleted zone, and that loss of KCBP function results in impairment of trichome branch initiation and elongation, and branch tip sharpening.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the comparison of wild-type and kcbp-1 mutant imaging data.

claim: Loss of KCBP function results in impairment of trichome branch initiation and elongation, and branch tip sharpening.
source: Together, these observations indicated that KCBP is required to assemble the transverse MT rings encircling the elongating branch and formation of the MT-depleted zone, and that loss of KCBP function results in impairment of trichome branch initiation and elongation, and branch tip sharpening.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the comparison of wild-type and kcbp-1 mutant imaging data.

claim: The parallel cytoplasmic actin cables, which extend along the long axis to the branch tip in wild-type trichomes, are disorganized in kcbp-1 trichomes.
source: Strikingly, the parallel cytoplasmic actin cables, which extend along the long axis to the branch tip in wild-type trichomes (Figure 4B–D), are disorganized in kcbp-1 trichomes, which instead have a curly, intertwined meshwork of thick actin bundles (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data comparing wild-type and kcbp-1 mutant trichomes.

claim: kcbp-1 trichomes have a curly, intertwined meshwork of thick actin bundles instead of parallel cytoplasmic actin cables.
source: Strikingly, the parallel cytoplasmic actin cables, which extend along the long axis to the branch tip in wild-type trichomes (Figure 4B–D), are disorganized in kcbp-1 trichomes, which instead have a curly, intertwined meshwork of thick actin bundles (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data comparing wild-type and kcbp-1 mutant trichomes.

claim: The transverse cortical F-actin cap, which is observed at the branch tip of elongating wild-type trichomes, is disrupted in kcbp-1 trichomes.
source: Moreover, the transverse cortical F-actin cap, which is observed at the branch tip of elongating wild-type trichomes (Figure 4C), is disrupted in kcbp-1 trichomes (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data comparing wild-type and kcbp-1 mutant trichomes.

claim: KCBP is implicated in the assembly of parallel cytoplasmic actin cables along the growth axis and the transverse cortical F-actin cap at the branch apex.
source: Taken together, these findings implicate KCBP in the assembly of parallel cytoplasmic actin cables along the growth axis and the transverse cortical F-actin cap at the branch apex, which are likely required for polarized branch elongation accompanied by tip sharpening, and further suggest that KCBP plays a critical role in regulating the MT-actin interaction.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the comparison of wild-type and kcbp-1 mutant imaging data.

claim: Parallel cytoplasmic actin cables along the growth axis and the transverse cortical F-actin cap at the branch apex are likely required for polarized branch elongation accompanied by tip sharpening.
source: Taken together, these findings implicate KCBP in the assembly of parallel cytoplasmic actin cables along the growth axis and the transverse cortical F-actin cap at the branch apex, which are likely required for polarized branch elongation accompanied by tip sharpening, and further suggest that KCBP plays a critical role in regulating the MT-actin interaction.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the comparison of wild-type and kcbp-1 mutant imaging data.

claim: KCBP plays a critical role in regulating the MT-actin interaction.
source: Taken together, these findings implicate KCBP in the assembly of parallel cytoplasmic actin cables along the growth axis and the transverse cortical F-actin cap at the branch apex, which are likely required for polarized branch elongation accompanied by tip sharpening, and further suggest that KCBP plays a critical role in regulating the MT-actin interaction.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the comparison of wild-type and kcbp-1 mutant imaging data.

claim: The construct without the motor domain could not rescue the trichome morphology of the kcbp-1 mutant.
source: As expected, the construct without the motor domain could not rescue the trichome morphology of the kcbp-1 mutant (Figure 5B)
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic complementation test data shown in figures.

claim: The construct without the C-terminal CBD domain could perfectly rescue the kcbp-1 trichome phenotype.
source: whereas the construct without the C-terminal CBD domain could perfectly rescue the kcbp-1 trichome phenotype (Figure 5B)
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic complementation test data shown in figures.

claim: The CBD domain is dispensable during trichome development.
source: whereas the construct without the C-terminal CBD domain could perfectly rescue the kcbp-1 trichome phenotype (Figure 5B), clearly indicating that the CBD domain is dispensable during trichome development.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the genetic complementation test data.

claim: Constructs with either the NT truncation or the MyTH4 truncation could rescue the kcbp-1 trichome morphology.
source: Furthermore, we found that constructs with either the NT truncation or the MyTH4 truncation could rescue the kcbp-1 trichome morphology, but the construct with a truncation of both NT and MyTH4 could not rescue the kcbp-1 trichome phenotype (Figure 5B).
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic complementation test data shown in figures.

claim: The construct with a truncation of both NT and MyTH4 could not rescue the kcbp-1 trichome phenotype.
source: Furthermore, we found that constructs with either the NT truncation or the MyTH4 truncation could rescue the kcbp-1 trichome morphology, but the construct with a truncation of both NT and MyTH4 could not rescue the kcbp-1 trichome phenotype (Figure 5B).
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic complementation test data shown in figures.

claim: Constructs with either truncation of the FERM domain or the (MyTH4+FERM) domains could rescue the kcbp-1 trichome morphology.
source: In addition, constructs with either truncation of the FERM domain or the (MyTH4+FERM) domains could rescue the kcbp-1 trichome morphology, but the construct containing a truncation of the whole (NT+MyTH4+FERM) could not rescue the kcbp-1 trichome morphology (Figure 5B).
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic complementation test data shown in figures.

claim: The construct containing a truncation of the whole (NT+MyTH4+FERM) could not rescue the kcbp-1 trichome morphology.
source: In addition, constructs with either truncation of the FERM domain or the (MyTH4+FERM) domains could rescue the kcbp-1 trichome morphology, but the construct containing a truncation of the whole (NT+MyTH4+FERM) could not rescue the kcbp-1 trichome morphology (Figure 5B).
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic complementation test data shown in figures.

claim: The NT and the MyTH4 domains are essential for trichome cell shape determination.
source: Importantly, these findings indicated that the NT and the MyTH4 domains are essential for trichome cell shape determination.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the genetic complementation test data.

claim: Rigor-KCBP exerted specific dominant-negative effects that resulted in more-severe trichome phenotypes.
source: Strikingly, the rigor-KCBP exerted specific dominant-negative effects that resulted in more-severe trichome phenotypes (Figure 6D,G–N), resembling a class of trichome mutants with defects in the actin cytoskeleton (Basu et al., 2004, 2005; Li et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2005a).
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic analysis data shown in figures and citations to previous literature.

claim: Rigor-KCBP trichome phenotypes resemble a class of trichome mutants with defects in the actin cytoskeleton.
source: Strikingly, the rigor-KCBP exerted specific dominant-negative effects that resulted in more-severe trichome phenotypes (Figure 6D,G–N), resembling a class of trichome mutants with defects in the actin cytoskeleton (Basu et al., 2004, 2005; Li et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2005a).
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic analysis data shown in figures and citations to previous literature.

claim: Most trichomes in plants expressing rigor-KCBP contained two branches but had an extremely twisted and swollen branch.
source: Most trichomes in plants expressing rigor-KCBP contained two branches but had an extremely twisted and swollen branch (Figure 6G–I)
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic analysis data shown in figures.

claim: Some rigor-KCBP trichomes had extremely elongated branches, more than two times as long as the wild-type control.
source: and some of them had extremely elongated branches, more than two times as long as the wild-type control (Figure 6M,N).
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic analysis data shown in figures.

claim: A small fraction of rigor-KCBP trichomes formed three branches but still contained one or two swollen and twisted branches.
source: Interestingly, a small fraction of trichomes formed three branches but still contained one or two swollen and twisted branches (Figure 6J–L).
evidence: This statement is supported by genetic analysis data shown in figures.

claim: More-severe abnormalities in the organization of both cortical MTs and F-actin were observed in rigor-KCBP trichomes when compared to the wild-type control.
source: Moreover, we observed more-severe abnormalities in the organization of both cortical MTs and F-actin in rigor-KCBP trichomes when compared to the wild-type control (Figure 6—figure supplement 1, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The typical, two-branched trichomes in zwichel mutants are aligned in a nearly parallel pattern on leaves, with the elongated and pointed branch toward the proximal part and another shortened and blunt-ended branch toward the distal part.
source: In addition, the typical, two-branched trichomes in zwichel mutants are aligned in a nearly parallel pattern on leaves, with the elongated and pointed branch toward the proximal part and another shortened and blunt-ended branch toward the distal part (Figure 6C) (Hülskamp et al., 1994; Oppenheimer et al., 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by imaging data shown in figures and citations to previous literature.

claim: In rigor-KCBP trichomes, the elongated and pointed branch toward the proximal part keeps unchanged, and the extremely swollen and twisting specifically takes place in another branch, which derives from the shortened and blunt-ended branch of the kcbp-1 background.
source: Notably, in rigor-KCBP trichomes, the elongated and pointed branch toward the proximal part keeps unchanged, and the extremely swollen and twisting specifically takes place in another branch, which derives from the shortened and blunt-ended branch of the kcbp-1 background (Figure 6D).
evidence: This statement is supported by imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The rigor-KCBP findings genetically supported the idea that KCBP participates in the organization of the actin cytoskeleton during trichome branching and elongation.
source: Collectively, these findings genetically supported the idea that KCBP participates in the organization of the actin cytoskeleton during trichome branching and elongation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the rigor-KCBP genetic analysis data.

claim: Either the NT or the MyTH4 domain can bind to MTs.
source: Single-molecule imaging showed that either the NT (amino acids 1–115) or the MyTH4 domain could bind to MTs, but the FERM domain did not bind MTs
evidence: This statement is supported by single-molecule imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The FERM domain did not bind MTs.
source: Single-molecule imaging showed that either the NT (amino acids 1–115) or the MyTH4 domain could bind to MTs, but the FERM domain did not bind MTs
evidence: This statement is supported by single-molecule imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The (NT+MyTH4) region and the (NT+MyTH4+FERM) region showed similar MT-binding activity to that of the single NT or MyTH4 domain.
source: the (NT+MyTH4) region and the (NT+MyTH4+FERM) region showed similar MT-binding activity to that of the single NT or MyTH4 domain
evidence: This statement is supported by single-molecule imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The motorless KCBP (NT+MyTH4+FERM+Coiled Coil) exhibited enhanced MT-binding activity and promoted the formation of MT bundles.
source: whereas the motorless KCBP (NT+MyTH4+FERM+Coiled Coil) exhibited enhanced MT-binding activity and promoted the formation of MT bundles (Figure 7A).
evidence: This statement is supported by single-molecule imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The FERM domain directly bound to F-actin.
source: Furthermore, the FERM domain directly bound to F-actin
evidence: This statement is supported by single-molecule imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The (NT+MyTH4+FERM) region showed similar F-actin-binding activity as the single FERM domain.
source: the (NT+MyTH4+FERM) region showed similar F-actin-binding activity as the single FERM domain
evidence: This statement is supported by single-molecule imaging data shown in figures.

claim: The motorless KCBP (NT+MyTH4+FERM+Coiled Coil) exhibited enhanced F-actin-binding and bundling activity.
source: whereas the motorless KCBP (NT+MyTH4+FERM+Coiled Coil) exhibited enhanced F-actin-binding and bundling activity (Figure 7B).
evidence: This statement is supported by single-molecule imaging data shown in figures.

claim: KCBP contains a second MT-binding domain spanning the NT and the MyTH4 region.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrated that KCBP contains a second MT-binding domain spanning the NT and the MyTH4 region, and can also bind to F-actin via the FERM domain, co-ordinating the interplay between MTs and F-actin.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the single-molecule imaging data.

claim: KCBP can bind to F-actin via the FERM domain.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrated that KCBP contains a second MT-binding domain spanning the NT and the MyTH4 region, and can also bind to F-actin via the FERM domain, co-ordinating the interplay between MTs and F-actin.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the single-molecule imaging data.

claim: KCBP coordinates the interplay between MTs and F-actin.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrated that KCBP contains a second MT-binding domain spanning the NT and the MyTH4 region, and can also bind to F-actin via the FERM domain, co-ordinating the interplay between MTs and F-actin.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the single-molecule imaging data.

claim: During trichome morphogenesis, KCBP forms a cortical gradient and highly accumulates at trichome-branching sites and apical regions of elongating branches, thus, integrating MTs and F-actin to assemble the required cytoskeletal configuration for trichome branching, elongation, and tip sharpening.
source: We propose that, during trichome morphogenesis, KCBP forms a cortical gradient and highly accumulates at trichome-branching sites and apical regions of elongating branches, thus, integrating MTs and F-actin to assemble the required cytoskeletal configuration for trichome branching, elongation, and tip sharpening (see the model in Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the combined data from imaging and biochemical assays.

claim: The introduction of the MyTH4-FERM tandem into KCBP during evolution conferred novel functions.
source: In this study, we show that introduction of the MyTH4-FERM tandem into KCBP (kinesin-like calmodulin-binding protein) during evolution conferred novel functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the functional characterization of KCBP domains.

claim: The MyTH4 domain in the N-terminal tail of KCBP physically binds to MTs.
source: The MyTH4 domain and the FERM domain in the N-terminal tail of KCBP physically bind to MTs and F-actin, respectively.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the single-molecule imaging data.

claim: The FERM domain in the N-terminal tail of KCBP physically binds to F-actin.
source: The MyTH4 domain and the FERM domain in the N-terminal tail of KCBP physically bind to MTs and F-actin, respectively.

claim: The introduction of the MyTH4-FERM domain into the N-terminal tail region of a Kinesin-14 motor during evolution conferred the novel functions of KCBP.
source: We propose that the introduction of the MyTH4-FERM domain into the N-terminal tail region of a Kinesin-14 motor during evolution conferred the novel functions of KCBP: the NT and the MyTH4 domain act synergistically to bind strongly to MTs, but still maintain the MT-binding activity of the individual domains, and the FERM domain carries out the novel actin-binding activity, thus, orchestrating the interaction between MTs and the actin cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the functional characterization of KCBP domains.

claim: KCBP is required for establishing the transverse MT rings to promote branch elongation.

claim: Through the FERM domain, KCBP may dominantly bind to cortical F-actin at higher density at the extreme apex.

This binding occurs at higher density at the extreme apex, as suggested by previous findings (Yang et al., 2009), and plays a critical role in the assembly of the F-actin cap, which then facilitates the maintenance of the MT-depleted zone to promote rapid elongation of trichome branches and tip sharpening (see model in Figure 7C).
